messages.text: Why is Championship cheat code Parker finding life tough at West Ham?

metadata.summary: The hope was that relegation would at least give West Ham the opportunity to reset, enjoy some winning football and, ideally, bounce straight back stronger. The reality, however, is proving rather different.
metadata.content: West Ham: Why Scott Parker is struggling to halt the slide after inheriting a host of problems | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis West Ham: Why Scott Parker is struggling to halt the slide after inheriting a host of problems West Ham on course for lowest finish since 1957 following six-game winless streak; Scott Parker unable to arrest slide of side accused of lacking leaders and character following Premier League relegation last season Ron Walker Football Journalist @Ronnabe Friday 27 November 2026 16:42, UK Image: Scott Parker replaced the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo at the beginning of November but is yet to win any of his four matches in charge The hope was that relegation would at least give West Ham the opportunity to reset, enjoy some winning football and, ideally, bounce straight back stronger. The reality, however, is proving rather different. There was a sense that, had Nuno Espirito Santo been given more time, he might have kept West Ham in the Premier League. After all, 25 points from the final 17 games of the season suggested he was beginning to steady the ship and that, with a little longer, he could have turned things around. Yet another 17 games later, Nuno is out of a job, while Scott Parker - a man who metaphorically bleeds claret and blue and boasts a formidable record in the Championship - has so far failed to make the anticipated impact as his replacement. metadata.content: Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunners sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off the top and have not won at home in the league all season Friday 27 November 2026 15:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Anton Toloui explains why Renee Slegers has been sacked by Arsenal following a poor start to the Women's Super League season. Renee Slegers has been sacked as Arsenal head coach after a poor start to the Women's Super League season. Slegers led Arsenal to Women's Champions League glory in May 2025 , having initially stepped up from assistant to Jonas Eidevall on an interim basis, then narrowly missed out on the WSL title to Manchester City in 2025/26. Such was her success at the time, the Dutchwoman signed a new contract with the club in January 2026, running until 2029. But a poor start to the 2026/27 campaign, in which Arsenal went on a five-game winless run in the WSL for the first time in their history, has culminated in Slegers' departure just 10 months into her new deal.
